summary: The study investigates the use of atomic layer deposition (ALD) to create biocompatible titanium nitride (TiN) coatings on cellulose fiber substrates. The process uses tetrakis(dimethylamido)titanium (TDMA T) and ammonia as precursors at low temperatures (<150 ◦C). The coatings are uniform and conformal, and their thickness influences cell adhesion properties. The study demonstrates the potential of low-temperature ALD for surface modification of cellulose and other implant materials.
evidence: Atomic layer deposition (ALD) is investigated as a process to produce inorganic metallic bio-adhesive coatings on cellulosic fiber substrates. ... In this study, we investigate ALD of TiN on cotton fibers and fabrics using TDMA T as the metal organic precursor source and NH3 as the reactant gas, where deposition temperature is maintained at less than 150 ◦C. ... The ALD process consists of a set of sequential, self-limiting deposition processes that operate on the principle of alternating saturating surface reactions. ... The study demonstrates the potential of low-temperature ALD as a surface modification technique to produce biocompatible cellulose and other implant materials.
